meta.note: Quotations are from the creed texts used on this page (Book of Common Prayer 1662 for the Apostles', Nicene and Athanasian Creeds; Schaff's translation of Chalcedon). 'In full' means the creed spells the point out; 'briefly' means it is affirmed without being defined; a gap means the creed does not address it.

creeds.added: The simplest outline of the faith: Father, Son and Spirit, the story of Jesus, and the hope of the resurrection. The only creed to mention the “communion of saints”.

creeds.purpose: Answering Arius: is the Son created?
creeds.added: Defines the Son as “of one substance with the Father”, “begotten, not made”; in 381 adds the Holy Spirit as “Lord and giver of life”, worshipped with the Father and the Son.

creeds.purpose: Answering Nestorius and Eutyches: how is Christ both God and man?
creeds.added: Not a creed for worship but a definition: one Christ “in two natures”, without confusion, change, division or separation. Calls Mary “Mother of God”.

creeds.purpose: Teaching the Trinity and the Incarnation in detail
creeds.added: The fullest statement of the Trinity (“one God in Trinity, and Trinity in Unity”) and of Christ’s two natures, framed by warnings that this faith is necessary for salvation.

rows.label: One God, the Father, Maker of all

apostles.q: I believe in God the Father Almighty, Maker of heaven and earth

nicene.q: I believe in one God the Father Almighty, Maker of heaven and earth, And of all things visible and invisible

athanasian.q: The Father is made of none: neither created, nor begotten.

rows.label: Three persons, one God
rows.note: Only the Athanasian Creed uses the words “Trinity” and “Persons”; the others name Father, Son and Spirit without defining how they are one.

apostles.q: God the Father … Jesus Christ his only Son … the Holy Ghost

nicene.q: Who with the Father and the Son together is worshipped and glorified

athanasian.q: We worship one God in Trinity, and Trinity in Unity; Neither confounding the Persons: nor dividing the Substance.

rows.label: Eternally begotten, truly God
rows.note: The heart of the Nicene Creed, written against Arius, who taught that the Son was created.

apostles.q: Jesus Christ his only Son our Lord

nicene.q: Begotten of his Father before all worlds, God of God, Light of Light, Very God of very God, Begotten, not made, Being of one substance with the Father

chalcedon.q: consubstantial with the Father according to the Godhead … begotten before all ages of the Father

athanasian.q: God, of the Substance of the Father, begotten before the worlds … Equal to the Father, as touching his Godhead

rows.label: Became man, born of the Virgin Mary

apostles.q: conceived by the Holy Ghost, Born of the Virgin Mary

nicene.q: was incarnate by the Holy Ghost of the Virgin Mary, And was made man

chalcedon.q: born of the Virgin Mary, the Mother of God, according to the Manhood

athanasian.q: Man, of the Substance of his Mother, born in the world

rows.label: Two natures in one person
rows.note: The question of Chalcedon. The Oriental Orthodox did not accept its wording, preferring “one united nature”.

nicene.q: Very God of very God … And was made man

chalcedon.q: to be acknowledged in two natures, inconfusedly, unchangeably, indivisibly, inseparably … concurring in one Person

athanasian.q: Who although he be God and Man: yet he is not two, but one Christ

rows.label: Mary called “Mother of God”
rows.note: The title (Theotokos) affirmed at Ephesus in 431 and repeated at Chalcedon: Mary bore the one person who is God.

chalcedon.q: the Virgin Mary, the Mother of God

apostles.q: Suffered under Pontius Pilate, Was crucified, dead, and buried

nicene.q: was crucified also for us under Pontius Pilate. He suffered and was buried

rows.label: Descended into hell
rows.note: Usually understood as Christ truly dying and entering the realm of the dead; the Nicene Creed omits it.

rows.label: Rose again on the third day

apostles.q: The third day he rose again from the dead

nicene.q: the third day he rose again according to the Scriptures

athanasian.q: rose again the third day from the dead

rows.label: Ascended, seated at God’s right hand

apostles.q: He ascended into heaven, And sitteth on the right hand of God the Father Almighty

nicene.q: ascended into heaven, And sitteth on the right hand of the Father

athanasian.q: He ascended into heaven, he sitteth on the right hand of the Father, God Almighty

apostles.q: From thence he shall come to judge the quick and the dead

nicene.q: he shall come again with glory to judge both the quick and the dead: Whose kingdom shall have no end

athanasian.q: from whence he shall come to judge the quick and the dead

apostles.q: I believe in the Holy Ghost

nicene.q: the Holy Ghost, The Lord and giver of life … Who with the Father and the Son together is worshipped and glorified, Who spake by the Prophets

athanasian.q: the Father is God, the Son is God: and the Holy Ghost is God. And yet they are not three Gods: but one God

rows.label: Proceeds from the Father “and the Son”
rows.note: The filioque. The Greek original of 381 says only “from the Father”; “and the Son” was added in the Latin West (Toledo, 589; Rome, 1014) and became a cause of the East–West Schism. The Eastern and Oriental Orthodox recite the creed without it.

nicene.q: Who proceedeth from the Father and the Son (Western text)

athanasian.q: The Holy Ghost is of the Father and of the Son: neither made, nor created, nor begotten, but proceeding

nicene.q: one Baptism for the remission of sins

rows.label: Resurrection of the body, eternal life

apostles.q: The Resurrection of the body, And the life everlasting

nicene.q: the Resurrection of the dead, And the life of the world to come

athanasian.q: all men shall rise again with their bodies … they that have done good shall go into life everlasting: and they that have done evil into everlasting fire

rows.label: Belief necessary for salvation
rows.note: The Athanasian Creed’s “warning” (damnatory) clauses. Some churches that receive the creed, such as many Anglican provinces, no longer read it in worship partly because of them.

athanasian.q: Whosoever will be saved: before all things it is necessary that he hold the Catholick Faith … without doubt he shall perish everlastingly.
